first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in brazil' to find out if it's even workable for two Australians who don't live there. The intro says yes and names the process, and the legal section cites the Public Registries Law with an 'as at' date. I jumped to the FAQ and cost section: the costs are all 'a fee applies' or 'ask', with no numbers. The real catch, the residence rule, is flagged honestly but never resolved. Smartraveller safety advice quoted straight, which I respect. Still nothing on what Wedded Wonderland charges or whether it takes a cut.

journey.section: Can foreigners legally marry in Brazil?
journey.quote: That residence wording is the first thing to raise with the cartório.
journey.reaction: So the law says the district where one of you resides, and we live in Brisbane. That's the catch. Credit for saying it, but the page hands the problem back to me. Can non-residents actually do this or not?

journey.quote: If the documents are in order, the registrar publishes your application electronically and issues the certificate of habilitação within up to 5 days.
journey.reaction: A number, tied to the law. Goes in the spreadsheet.

journey.section: Public notice and how long approval lasts
journey.quote: How many days in Brazil should we allow between arriving and the ceremony?
journey.reaction: That's the question I came here to have answered, and it's on a list of things for me to ask someone else. How long the proclamas runs and how long the clearance lasts are the same: questions, not answers.

journey.quote: In Brazil, foreign documents, even when apostilled, must be translated by a tradutor juramentado, a sworn public translator, to be valid, and that translation can only be done in Brazil.
journey.reaction: Real trap, stated up front. Exactly what I'd want to know before booking flights.

journey.quote: Embassy staff will not say which documents you need, and a CNI application mailed from within Brazil is accepted only if a local notary at a cartório witnessed the signature.
journey.reaction: Unflattering detail most wedding sites would leave out. Trust up.

journey.section: A religious ceremony with civil effect
journey.quote: The rituals around the day are a separate pleasure.

It says violent crime including mugging, armed robbery and carjacking is common, more often in large cities and during festivals such as Carnival, and advises against going out alone at night and against isolated areas, including beaches.
journey.reaction: A wedding business quoting government crime advice instead of hiding it. Sourced and plain. This is the honesty I look for.

journey.quote: Deposits: whose name is on the contract, and when do deposits become non-refundable?
journey.reaction: The question I got burned on last time. Good to see it.

journey.section: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
journey.quote: On the paperwork side, a fee applies for an Australian CNI and for the Embassy's notarial services.
journey.reaction: The cost section has zero numbers. Not the CNI fee, which DFAT publishes, not a cartório range, not a translator rate per page, not a rough 'from AUD' for a Brazil wedding. A cost heading with no costs.

journey.section: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
journey.quote: If you would like the whole picture costed on your own dates, ask Wedded Concierge.
journey.reaction: Sales link at the exact point where the page should have given me numbers. Feels like the numbers are the bait.

journey.quote: Smartraveller names Copacabana Beach, Ipanema Beach, the Pedra do Sal area, Santa Teresa, Lapa, the Christ the Redeemer statue and the Corcovado Trail as crime hotspots.
journey.reaction: Naming the postcard spots as hotspots is honest. Useful for planning photos.

journey.quote: Paraty is on the Visit Brasil list alongside Búzios.
journey.reaction: That tells me nothing. No airport, transfer time or accommodation. The region section is a tourism list.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you as one point of contact from start to finish, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing is fine, but payments through you is where I ask: do you take a cut from the venue? And have you actually done a Brazil wedding? No real wedding, no budget, nothing.

journey.section: Plan your Brazil wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Everything around it is where the planning begins.

turn_offs_found.quote: On the paperwork side, a fee applies for an Australian CNI and for the Embassy's notarial services.
turn_offs_found.why: A cost section with no costs. Government fees are published, yet none are given, and there's no ballpark for the wedding itself. Unquantified costs look like the catch.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would like the whole picture costed on your own dates, ask Wedded Concierge.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA lands before any evidence on cost, right where numbers should be.

turn_offs_found.quote: The rituals around the day are a separate pleasure.
Paraty is on the Visit Brasil list alongside Búzios.
turn_offs_found.why: Brochure-style listing with no practical facts (airport, transfer time, cost) I could use to choose.

turn_offs_found.quote: Everything around it is where the planning begins.
turn_offs_found.why: Mood line with no content on a page that otherwise earns trust with sourced facts.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the sworn-translation-only-in-Brazil rule, the 5-day habilitação and the 30-day registration window for a religious ceremony
Our Reddit thread: the Smartraveller safety points and the venue deposit and security questions

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor stays with you from start to finish, works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: The legal and safety content is sourced and honest, so I trust the page more than most. But the residence question, the time-in-country question and every cost are left open, and nothing says how you're paid or whether you take a cut. I'd email those questions before booking a call.

top_3_changes: Resolve the non-resident question: state plainly what the source says about foreign couples who don't live in Brazil applying for the habilitação; if it's not published, say so and put it first on the checklist.
Put numbers in the cost section: the published DFAT CNI and notarial fees with an 'as at' date, and a minimum days-in-Brazil estimate if sourced; move the Concierge link below them.

Answer the proclamas length and habilitação validity from the Civil Code instead of listing them as questions; cut mood lines ('a separate pleasure', 'Everything around it is where the planning begins') and add airport or transfer facts to regions if the source pack allows.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and cost first, looked for the catch and the numbers, flagged emotional language and early CTAs
No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, real weddings and ground team listed as deferred unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

If yes, the residence, timing and cost objections close with sourced lines; if not, 'not published' plus a checklist item is the fallback.
